label: HTTP endpoint to WhatsApp
info: Any system can send a WhatsApp message with one HTTP call: POST /whatsapp/alert.

name: START HERE: setup in 3 steps (select this note)
info:
**Setup in 3 steps** (once, about five minutes)

1. **Link your WhatsApp number.** In the [Turbo Notify dashboard](https://dashboard.turbonotify.com) create an account if you have none (it is free), then open **Numbers** and connect your WhatsApp number. First time? Follow the [step by step guide](https://docs.turbonotify.com/en/guides/quickstart/).
2. **Create an API key.** Open **API keys** and create one with the **AI agent (MCP)** template. Copy it, it is shown only once. This flow uses the scope messages:send.
3. **Paste it here.** Double-click a whatsapp node of this flow, click the pencil next to **Account**, paste the key and press **Test**. It tells you whether the key works and whether your number is linked.

**About this flow.** First set the variable ALERT_TOKEN of this tab (double-click the tab, then Environment variables) to a long random string of at least 16 characters: until you do, the endpoint refuses every call with 503. Then call it with: curl -X POST http://localhost:1880/whatsapp/alert -H 'x-token: YOUR_TOKEN' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"to":"+12025550123","message":"Backup finished"}'. Whoever holds the token can send a message to any number from your number, so keep it secret and serve Node-RED over https. The answer is 202 with the message id, 400 for a bad body, 401 for a wrong token, 503 while no token is set and 502 when Turbo Notify refuses the message.
